title: Deep Avatar (Stage 5) — האווטאר העמוק
description: Output of stage-5-deep-avatar per doctrine/14: six layers, 24 fields, each field anchor-tagged (Anchoring Law): 'quote' [ציטוט] / 'category_inference' [היסק-קטגוריה] / 'unknown' [לא ידוע]. Empty beats pretty. This is the SEGMENT avatar; the per-ad mini-avatar lives in the memo (field 2b).

segment_name.description: The stage-4 segment this avatar maps.

identity.description: Layer A — identity and life picture (fields 1-3).

portrait.description: 1. One person — name, age, life situation. Not a segment.

week_texture.description: 2. The concrete moments where the problem stings — which day, where, in front of whom.

identity_gap.description: 3. 'Who I am' vs 'who I became' — what the problem stole from her self-story. Feeds: identity angles.

fear_ladder.description: 4. Three floors. The ad works one floor BELOW where competitors work.

three_am_thoughts.description: 5. What she tells no one. Feeds: confession hooks, 'how did you know' lines.

shame_and_hiding.description: 6. What she hides, from whom, and the LOGISTICS of hiding (the objects! the excuses!). Feeds: sensory details that make 'a real person wrote this'.

dreams.description: 7. Three levels. Feeds: the transformation arc, the story's payoff.

envy_comparison.description: 8. Who she measures herself against, and what about the other woman pinches. Feeds: social-proof and identification angles.

cause_theory.description: 9. Why SHE thinks it happened to her (right or wrong — this is the belief the copy meets).

who_is_blamed.description: 10. Herself / age / doctors / her body. Feeds: whom the ad absolves — the gold move of health categories.

solution_beliefs.description: 11. What she believes about the category ('supplements = scam'; 'it's just part of aging' — the fatalism belief is almost always the belief-to-shift).

past_attempts_scars.description: 12. What she tried, why she thinks it failed, and the trust scar left. Feeds: differentiation must answer THE specific scar.

entry_point_note.description: 13. What this dictates for the entry point.

already_seen.description: 14. Her ad-fatigue in this category: which promises no longer work on her. Cross-references the stage-2 saturation map.

consumer_trust_wounds.description: 15. The purchase that disappointed, the signup that drowned her in spam. Feeds: what NOT to do + trust signals.

stated_vs_real_objection.description: 16. 'Does it work?' (stated) vs 'I can't survive another disappointment' (real). The ad answers the real one THROUGH the stated one.

purchase_context.description: 17. Who sees the package, who sees the credit-card charge, how much discretion she needs. Critical in shame categories.

internal_price_anchor.description: 18. What she compares the amount to in her head. Feeds: the price-anchor function in the closing engine.

permission_needed.description: 19. What someone must tell her so she allows herself to believe it can be different. Feeds: the ad's turning line.

decision_moment.description: 20. When and where she clicks (at night in bed? after an embarrassing event?). Feeds: tone, timing, urgency.

action_fields.description: Layer F — action fields: conclusions, not data (fields 21-24).

voc_lines.description: 21. Lines in THEIR words, each source-tagged.

the_one_trigger.description: 22. The single deepest emotion everything drains into.

forbidden_word.description: 24. What must never be said to her (what triggers the defenses). No less important than what to say.

anchor_tag.description: The Anchoring Law: quote=[ציטוט] (real stage-3 source) · category_inference=[היסק-קטגוריה] (reasoned, marked) · unknown=[לא ידוע] (empty beats pretty). Fabricated quotes presented as real = violation.

value.description: The field content. null ONLY when anchor='unknown'.

source.description: Required (non-null) when anchor='quote'. For 'category_inference': the reasoning basis. null for 'unknown'.
